title: Tottenham sign Mykhailo Mudryk on loan from Chelsea, with £75m buy option
content:
Tottenham Hotspur have completed a deal to sign Mykhailo Mudryk on loan from Chelsea until the end of the season.

The north London side have the option to make the move permanent for a fee of £75million.

The Athletic reported on Monday that Spurs had enquired about Mudryk. They have also agreed a deal to sign centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, marking the first time that a player has moved directly between the two clubs since 2009, when goalkeeper Carlo Cudicini joined Spurs.

Mudryk is set to be reunited with Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi, having starred under the Italian at Shakhtar Donetsk.

“I’m so excited to be reunited with Roberto De Zerbi,” Mudryk told Spurs’ club website.

“I’m a player who brings speed and creativity, and I want to help in both the offensive and defensive areas. I want to make the fans excited.

“I can see it’s a strong squad here with good players, and I’m looking forward to sharing a pitch and special moments with them.”

De Zerbi said: “I will demand a lot from Misha and it is our job to help him find the best version of himself. If we do that then he can become a very important player for us. I am very happy he chose to come here, and I cannot wait to work with him again.”

The 25-year-old last played a competitive game for Chelsea in November 2024, having returned an adverse finding in a urine sample and received a four-year ban, the English Football Association’s maximum penalty for doping, which he was appealing at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

On July 31, a resolution between the FA and World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) was reached over an anti-doping violation, allowing Mudryk to return to club training and selection. He featured in three of the club’s pre-season friendlies but was not included in the squad for any of Chelsea’s first three competitive games of the campaign.

Spurs pivoted to Mudryk after pursuing Cody Gakpo, who is set to stay at Liverpool, and Iliman Ndiaye, who has joined Manchester City in a £65m deal.

Mudryk has appeared 73 times for Chelsea, scoring 10 goals, in a €100million (£85.5m; $116.7m) move from Shakhtar in January 2023.

Tottenham have had an extremely busy window, with Mudryk their ninth arrival of the summer and Adarabioyo set to be number 10. They have spent in excess of £300m bringing in the Sandro Tonali, Jan Paul van Hecke, Mateus Fernandes and Savio for hefty transfer fees. Omar Marmoush has arrived on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent, while Martin Dubravka, Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi have joined on free transfers.
